End of Project Evaluation. UNDP in consultation with Judiciary the Delegation of European Union the Government and key stakeholders commissioned external end of project evaluation. The end of project evaluation was conducted by an independent consultant whose results were publicly validated by key stakeholders. Based on UNDP and OECD evaluation framework the evaluation assessed the extent to which the Support to Implementation of the Justice Sector Reforms Project had met its objectives to provide evidence of UNDPs contribution towards outcome achievements and role played by and partnerships developed for purposes of informing future programming actions. The specific elements of the evaluation were to a establish to extent to which the planned and related project objectives outcomes and results of the project had been achieved b the relevance efficiency and effectiveness of the project in achieving its objectives outcomes and results c assess factors affecting the project implementation outputs and its sustainability contributing factors and constraints d assess UNDPs strategy used in making contribution to the outcome including use of partnerships for implementation and programming arrangements e examine the extent to which gender and human rights were considered in the projects design implementation and monitoring f establish lessons learnt from project implementation and g make recommendations for improving design effectiveness efficiency and sustainability for future programming.
